title: Vega OS implementation guide
lead: Use the current code to connect Kepler and native media, configure the Player, and implement remote UI, subtitles and Analytics.

blocks.text: Connect the modular Player to Vega media
blocks.summary: Connect the modular Player to Kepler’s native media and video surface, preserving initialization order and session release across app state changes.

blocks.text: The Vega app runs the Vega-compatible modular Bitmovin Web SDK in Amazon’s Kepler runtime. Its setup differs from Android-based Fire TV and bitmovin-player-react-native. Kepler renders the React Native screen; @amazon-devices/react-native-w3cmedia supplies native media objects and the video surface. Use the pinned versions in apps/vega/package.json. The official sample also specifies a supported release line distinct from the general browser Player.
Prepare the Kepler host and native surface

items: Follow Build the Kepler application in the Vega README to build and launch the existing host. The app ID is com.playerlab.vega and its main component is com.playerlab.vega.main. After a license change, regenerate the ignored runtime configuration and rebuild.
App.tsx retains applied PlayerConfig and SourceConfig and passes them to BitmovinPlayer. Drafts are separate, so incomplete edits do not affect playback.

BitmovinPlayer.tsx receives the current surface handle from KeplerVideoSurfaceView. It starts a session only while the app is foregrounded, with a current handle and after the previous session has been released.

items.label: Vega README: build the Kepler host

blocks.text: TextInput uses Vega’s on-screen keyboard. manifest.toml declares com.amazon.inputmethod.service in wants.service so it can open on devices and Vega Virtual Device.
A minimal player in the existing host

This example uses Player Lab’s existing Kepler host and helpers. Replace the key and HLS URL, and allow com.playerlab.vega on the Player license. Replace apps/vega/src/App.tsx with the line below to expose the example as the named App export loaded by index.js. The SDK’s public constructor type requires HTMLElement, so the existing createVegaPlayer adapter provides the Vega connection.

blocks.title: src/App.tsx in the existing host
blocks.text: export { default as App } from "../examples/MinimalPlayer";

blocks.title: Create the display target and session, handle errors and release

blocks.text: startVegaSession manages VideoPlayer initialization, handle attachment, SDK creation and load, and release of the Player and native media. Entering the background starts synchronous native release. Returning to the foreground creates a new surface and session, waiting for the previous session’s release before initialization.

PlaybackController displays the playback position; Text shows initialization and playback errors. The app’s BitmovinPlayer.tsx uses the same createVegaPlayer adapter, polyfills and session management. The excerpts below show the SDK calls inside these helpers.
Initialize native media and manage its lifecycle

items: playerSession.ts initializes VideoPlayer, attaches the surface, installs media compatibility APIs, creates the modular Player, registers events and loads SourceConfig, in that order. Preserve this sequence when extending the host.

blocks.title: Initialize native media before constructing and loading the SDK Player

blocks.text: startVegaSession and createVegaPlayer are app helpers. VideoPlayer.initialize and setSurfaceHandle are Amazon media APIs; Player.addModule, new Player and Player.load belong to the Bitmovin Web SDK. BitmovinPlayer.tsx supplies the creation, event and controller callbacks in the excerpt. This code is part of the existing host.

blocks.title: Create the modular SDK Player without a browser container

blocks.text: vegaPlayer.ts registers the ReactNative media integration and modules for formats, rendering, adaptation, subtitles and DRM. polyfills.ts connects Amazon’s MediaSource, HTMLMediaElement and WebCrypto with XML and Base64 compatibility helpers. The session-owned gvideo connects the SDK to the current native VideoPlayer.

blocks.title: Available Web APIs
blocks.text: The compatibility layer does not create a browser document or HTML UI. Configuration fields do not supply DOM elements, canvas/WebGL VR, browser UI factories, Cast receivers or device sensors. A plain object cannot replace a real HTML element required by a callback. Check host support separately from the presence of a field in the SDK types.

When the app moves to the background, the host releases native media before suspension. Returning to the foreground starts a replacement session with the retained configuration and source; it does not restore the previous position. A replacement waits for the previous owner’s release before using the global media adapters.
Change PlayerConfig and SourceConfig
blocks.summary: Map inputs to the Web SDK’s PlayerConfig and SourceConfig, keep Fetch transport and apply typed settings through the current native session.

blocks.text: PlayerConfig uses Web SDK fields such as playback, buffer and adaptation; SourceConfig selects media through hls, dash or progressive. parseConfiguration builds basic settings, then VegaSessionApi.prepare converts typed overrides and allowed functions. The result is used for Player creation and source loading.
Map the basic configuration fields

blocks.title: Map basic playback, buffer and bitrate inputs

rows: Autoplay and initial mute
PlayerConfig.playback.autoplay / muted
Apply at startup of a new Player. Both app defaults are on. Use PlayerAPI.play, pause and other commands during playback.
Audio/video buffer targets
PlayerConfig.buffer.audio.forwardduration / video.forwardduration

Positive finite seconds. Blank uses the SDK default of 40 seconds each for audio and video. Live playlists and available media can limit actual buffering; check the target content and device. These fields do not extend the rewind window.
Video bitrate cap
PlayerConfig.adaptation.bitrates.maxSelectableVideoBitrate
A positive value in bit/s; blank leaves the cap unset. It limits selection among supplied qualities and cannot add a missing quality.
Media address
SourceConfig.hls / dash / progressive
The selected format key receives the HTTP/HTTPS URL; progressive uses a URL string. Check the format, container and codec combination on the target device.
Title, poster and start position
SourceConfig.title / poster / options.startOffset / startOffsetTimelineReference

title and poster are metadata; this screen does not render a poster. The start offset is a signed finite decimal in seconds. Start refers to the media or live-window beginning; End refers to its end or the live edge. The SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live.
External WebVTT subtitles
SourceConfig.subtitleTracks
Supply an HTTPS URL reachable from the device, a label and a language tag such as en-US. Activate with enabled on load or PlayerAPI.subtitles. The app renders plain cue text in a native overlay.

blocks.text: Build source data for the selected format

blocks.title: Map media format, subtitles and start options to SourceConfig

blocks.text: media is the app object containing the selected hls, dash or progressive URL. Subtitle lang, id and enabled are Web SDK fields, distinct from the React Native wrapper’s language, identifier and isDefault. The validated source loads after native media and the surface are connected.
Apply configuration through the native session

blocks.title: Keep Fetch as the native transport

blocks.text: vegaPlayerConfig always merges requestApi: Fetch into network settings. This host has no XHR media transport, so the form rejects XHR before Apply. Other network callbacks belong in PlayerConfig.network.

items: Apply validates the whole draft, releases the previous session, creates a new Player and loads the source. Source, configuration or extra-input changes replace the session without restoring its position. Reset draft does not affect playback.
Overrides follow exact PlayerConfig/SourceConfig paths and SDK types. Related required fields in objects, maps and arrays can be edited together before Apply.

Check function arguments and return requirements, then allow execution before Apply. SDK callbacks run when invoked by the SDK; allowed value factories can also run during Apply, API preparation or recreation of an allowed session. Factories for any values may run during preparation. JavaScript executes inside the app without a sandbox.

Binary inputs such as certificates decode hexadecimal or Base64 into buffers or typed arrays. Fields requiring SDK instances must use objects obtained through real SDK APIs in the current session, rather than plain-object substitutes.

blocks.text: Overrides replace basic-form values; removing one restores the form or SDK default. A SourceConfig.subtitleTracks array replaces the single-track form. Applied code shows values and allowed function bodies, using placeholders for licenses and sensitive headers. Accepting an input does not by itself establish working behavior on native video.

blocks.caption: Applied configuration shown by the existing Vega app. D-pad focus allows the code lines to scroll into view; there is no clipboard integration.

blocks.text: Save and reuse named configuration drafts

items: Edit the settings to keep under Show configuration, then choose Saved configurations.
Enter a configuration name and choose Save draft. A duplicate name requires confirmation before replacement.

Choose Select saved configuration, select an item and choose Load draft. Review the draft, then choose Apply and recreate player. Saving or loading alone does not call the SDK, reload the source or change playback.
Use Delete saved configuration to remove the selected item after confirmation. Saved items remain available after restarting this app.

rows: Basic settings
Source format, initial offset and reference, autoplay, mute, audio/video forward buffers and maximum video bitrate.
Built-in sources
A preset ID is saved only when its public URL and format exactly match a built-in source. Custom URLs are not saved; without a preset, loading keeps the current URL.
Detailed settings

Explicitly supported numeric, toggle and enum values for playback, buffering, adaptation, live playback and selected UI or tweak settings. configurationProfiles.ts defines the full allowlist. Finite numeric editor inputs are saved as numbers. Other editor input objects are excluded.
Excluded fields

Player, Analytics and DRM keys; credentials and headers; custom URLs, titles and other free text; subtitles, lists, callbacks, scripts, metadata and runtime resources. Loading keeps their current draft values.

blocks.text: Restoration replaces the saved subset as a set. If a supported detailed setting was unset when saved, loading removes a later override and returns that field to its SDK default. Excluded current fields remain unchanged. Names are normalized to NFC, the standard composed Unicode form, and limited to 1–48 Unicode code points; collections are limited to 20 items, 8 KiB per item and 128 KiB in total. Unsupported schema versions, platforms, fields, types or corrupt data produce an error. A different SDK version requires confirmation after validating the supported fields; it is not automatically applied.

blocks.title: Restore editor data without applying Player configuration

blocks.text: The Vega host stores validated JSON under its own Kepler AsyncStorage key. It never clears other application or SDK storage. Storage errors leave the current draft and playback unchanged. These values are not encrypted by this feature and may be included in operating-system backups. No account API or network request is needed to save or load them.
Customize the native layout and remote controls
blocks.summary: Change Kepler’s native layout, subtitle overlay and controls while keeping each action reachable by remote focus.

blocks.text: App.tsx defaults to ui: false, placing BitmovinPlayer above a ScrollView with ControlPanel, SDK API operations and ConfigurationPanel. Change the UI through React Native components and StyleSheet. The host has no bitmovin-player-ui; PlayerConfig.ui or a browser theme does not create HTML controls.
Change the native layout and subtitle overlay

blocks.title: Keep the native surface and render subtitle text over it

rows: Resize the video and panel areas
BitmovinPlayer styles.video uses height: 50%; its surface fills the parent. App’s root uses flex: 1.
Adjust the native view dimensions together with the remaining settings area. Retain the current surface callback and handle binding; screen size changes do not replace that media connection.
Change how the image fits
KeplerVideoSurfaceView receives scalingmode="fit".
Use the values supported by the installed Amazon surface API when changing this prop. Player source poster/title fields do not control this native surface’s layout.
Restyle subtitle text
BitmovinPlayer’s captions and cue styles set the native overlay position, color, background and font.
Edit those StyleSheet entries. This renderer shows plain cue text; it does not implement WebVTT layout, HTML styling or the browser subtitle settings menu.

blocks.caption: The existing Vega app draws an external WebVTT cue as native text over the video. The surrounding controls are Kepler components, not the browser Player UI.

blocks.text: Keep remote focus and control actions connected

rows: Change control layout
ControlPanel.tsx composes rows using the localized Button wrapper and the Allow DVR Switch. The wrapper renders a focusable Pressable, with consistent text size, spacing and focus borders.

Edit these rows or the shared button styles in localization.tsx. Keep onPress, disabled state and the native D-pad focus path connected. On the tested Vega SDK, disabled controls received focus even with focusable=false. Keep their disabled appearance and focus indicator visible, and verify that Select performs no action. The input editors use the same visible focus treatment.
Connect a control to playback
The existing Live edge button calls controllerRef.current?.goToLiveEdge(); seek buttons use the same current controller.
Use the active controller or current SDK session for an added action. Compare its event/state result; do not retain a Player resource from an earlier session.

blocks.title: Make a native switch reachable by remote focus
blocks.text:
<Switch
          focusable
          style={styles.toggle}
          accessibilityLabel="Allow DVR"
          value={dvrAllowed}
          onValueChange={(v) => {
            onDvrAllowedChange(v);
            controllerRef.current?.setTimeShiftEnabled(v);
          }}
        />

After a layout change, check D-pad access to switches, code below the video and collapsible editors. Amazon’s focus guide explains how control positions affect navigation. Verify native focus behavior when adapting a touch layout to TV.
Try subtitles, SDK operations and HLS insertion
blocks.summary: Call the installed SDK, render native subtitle cues and try HLS insertion using content and device capabilities suited to each feature.

blocks.text: Run operations on the current SDK session

The API panel passes typed arguments to the installed PlayerAPI. Inspect current SDK API availability checks method presence and current source, live-window and ad prerequisites without calling commands. The selector and dispatch share the same checks; dispatch repeats them after materializing arguments. Source changes preserve the selected command and draft. After execution, inspect state, events and the picture. HLS track operations require HLS; DASH period operations require DASH.

getSource() can retain a configuration after Error. VegaSessionApi keeps a separate failure state even when event recording is paused; SourceLoaded or a successful recovery load clears it, while a newer Error during that load stays recorded. Drafts such as numbers, strings and source-configuration data survive source replacement. SDK object references remain tied to their original session and must be selected again if expired.

items: For audio, call PlayerAPI.getAvailableAudio and pass a returned track ID to PlayerAPI.setAudio. Compare PlayerAPI.getAudio with the audible output. For quality and buffer experiments, compare current values and playback after the operation. A source with one quality or one audio track cannot demonstrate switching.

For low-latency controls, use a suitable live stream and compare target/readback and actual behavior. On VOD, a setter may be accepted while latency remains zero. A registered module does not make every source or device support its feature.

blocks.text: lab.getPlayer() and lab.getSource() resolve the current session. Return the published SDK type and obtain native objects from a real SDK API; an object literal cannot create an SDK instance or an HTML container. Callback outcomes are logged without request payloads. PlayerAPI.off needs the same callback instance passed to on, so select that actual resource from the current SDK session. Event summaries are bounded and credential fields are redacted; callbacks from retired sessions are ignored.

blocks.caption: PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime executed during playback. Read the return value together with changing video frames and SDK events.

blocks.text: Render subtitle cues in native text

items: For external subtitles, configure a WebVTT URL, label and language and enable the track on load. After Apply, use PlayerAPI.subtitles.list and PlayerAPI.subtitles.enable with the track ID when needed. Play through a matching cue interval and inspect CueEnter/CueExit events.

blocks.title: Observe subtitle cues in the native text adapter

blocks.text: attachSubtitleDisplay is the app’s text renderer. It tracks active cue text, removes cues on CueExit, clears the overlay when subtitles are disabled and detaches its event callbacks on disposal. This is why configuring a track and rendering its cues are separate parts of the integration.
Handle insertion markers in HLS

items: For HLS interstitials, select a source that actually contains insertion markers and enable PlayerConfig.tweaks.enable_sgai_handling. PlayerAPI.sgai.list returns its schedule; getActiveAd is normally empty outside an insertion. Try skip only while applicable and compare AdStarted, AdSkipped, AdBreakFinished and playback.

blocks.text: SGAI means server-guided ad insertion: it follows markers in the HLS source, unlike client-side ad integration. If an insertion falls outside the media window, compare the source’s program date time with the insertion start time.

blocks.title: Content and device prerequisites
blocks.text: The app registers DRM/crypto and additional format modules; compatible encrypted media, licenses and decoding capabilities are still required. The official Vega sample excludes the HTML Player UI and client-side ads and documents constraints on server-side ad content. This host also has no client-side ad integration; its SGAI flow needs appropriate HLS. Feature support differs between general Web, Android-based Fire TV and Vega.
FAQ and troubleshooting
blocks.summary: Diagnose native surface, transport, lifecycle, subtitle and licensing issues without confusing Vega with a browser or Android Fire TV integration.

rows: Why do browser UI settings have no visible effect?
Kepler has no HTML Player UI. Keep ui: false and change native components and styles. See integration for Web API support and the UI chapter for layout and controls.
Why does XHR fail?
The media adapter requires Fetch and the form rejects other transport choices. Retain vegaPlayerConfig and the installed native media/polyfill initialization.
Why is the video black before readiness?

The native VideoPlayer must initialize and receive the current surface handle before SDK creation/load. Inspect setup/source errors and confirm that the app is active and the surface callback has arrived. A successful JavaScript build alone does not establish a working native surface.
Why does Apply or returning from the background reset playback?
The app replaces the session and reloads the retained source/configuration. It does not restore playback position. Background handling releases native media before the app can be suspended.
What if cleanup is unconfirmed?

Inactive status means that the owner no longer accepts SDK calls; it does not report completion of native cleanup. Recreate Vega player waits for the existing cleanup barrier before starting another owner. Restart the app if native player release or initialization cancellation is unconfirmed. Repeated Apply cannot confirm release.
Why are subtitles configured but not drawn?

Enable the external track on load or select its current ID, use cue times that overlap playback and inspect CueEnter. The renderer handles plain cue text; browser-specific styling and layout need their own native implementation.
Why does a licensed build still reject the app?

Allowlist com.playerlab.vega on the license in use, regenerate the ignored runtime configuration and rebuild the package. Runtime configuration is embedded before App is evaluated; editing the root file alone does not update an installed package.
Can the general browser SDK or a mocked test prove Vega support?

No. Keep the Vega-specific dependency and compare the official limitations. Unit tests can check validation and ordering, while native build, remote interaction, video and feature behavior require the target runtime.

blocks.text: Analytics / Observability
blocks.summary: Configure the Vega collector and source labels, then find the corresponding playback sessions and metrics in Bitmovin Dashboard.

blocks.text: Configure collection and source metadata

vegaPlayer.ts registers the Analytics module. App.tsx adds analytics.key only when BITMOVIN_ANALYTICS_LICENSE_KEY is configured, independently of the Player license. The final PlayerConfig and SourceConfig pass through VegaSessionApi.prepare, so Show all SDK configuration can also supply supported Analytics properties and source labels. Use PlayerConfig.analytics for collector configuration and SourceConfig.analytics for source-level metadata such as videoId, title or customData1.

blocks.title: Add the optional collector to the existing Player configuration

blocks.text: tweaks.app_id in this fragment identifies the Player app for licensing; it is not an Analytics content identifier. The constructor receives the optional collector key, while source metadata travels with the source loaded later. The API catalog follows the installed Vega SDK surface, which differs from the React Native wrapper’s analyticsConfig and analyticsSourceMetadata names. Do not copy one platform’s configuration path into the other.
Find playback sessions in Dashboard

items: Use an Analytics license authorized for the Vega app and non-sensitive videoId and experiment labels. After changing a key, regenerate runtime configuration and rebuild before playback.

In Dashboard, select the matching Analytics license, period and content/app filters, then match the playback session to SDK events. Use the shared guides below for metrics, aggregation and visualization. Keep account API credentials in trusted server-side tools; a collector license alone does not grant aggregate API access.
